title: Morph
description: One black pill on warm white that is the whole player. At rest it is a capsule with the cover, the elapsed time and a waveform tinted from the record. Click it and two objects carry the open on one spring: the cover grows out of its own corner from a thumbnail into a sleeve, and the pill's small elapsed time rises beside it and grows, redrawn as real type at every size with the tracking that size calls for, into the headline figures of a flush-left type column. Open, there is no app chrome, only the sleeve and the type. The figures are the scrubber: drag them sideways to seek, and each tabular figure rolls on its own spring like an odometer drum, cut off at the figures' own baseline. Progress is a single hairline laid on that baseline across the full measure, played in full ink and the rest in the secondary ink, with the time left standing at its far end; tap the sleeve to pause, and the colon blinks like a stopped clock. A few seconds before a song ends the pill reshapes on its own into a wider toast announcing the next one, then folds back. Nothing is a new sheet: width, height and corner radius run on one spring from wherever they are, so you can change your mind mid-morph; the waveform folds flat in place and goes, everything else fades through a slight blur as the edge reveals or absorbs it, and the corners stay continuous curves from capsule to squircle.
intent: Translate the one-surface morph of Emil Kowalski's Dynamic Island recreation (https://emilkowal.ski/ui/dynamic-island) and Family's dynamic tray (https://benji.org/family-values) into a now-playing control: states are shapes of one object on interruptible springs, shared elements travel, the rest crossfades with blur so nothing pops.
